children: Cummins Inc. (NYSE:CMI) sees robust H2 2026 North American truck demand and extended QSK95 orders into 2028, while passing NCP costs into legacy pricing that keeps profits flat but trims margins; the firm shifts capital to batteries, efficiency products and aftermarket growth, warning of potential margin dilution.
Cummins Inc. Expects Strong North American Truck Demand
: Cummins (CMI) expects strong North American truck demand in H2 2026, cites better fleet profitability, 2027 emissions rule clarity, planned 2027 cost increases, and new efficiency-focused products.
CMI To Cover NCP Costs Via Higher Prices
: Cummins (CMI) says NCP-related costs will be covered by higher prices on legacy products, keeping profit dollars flat but reducing profit margins percentage-wise due to pass-through pricing.
Multiyear Hyperscale Deal; QSK95 Orders Extend
: Cummins (CMI) renewed a multiyear deal with a hyperscale data‑center client; QSK95 generator orders now extend into H2 2028. Supply limits pushed some buyers to smaller engines.
Battery Storage For Data Centers Revenue
: Cummins (CMI) targets battery energy storage for data centers to balance grid load; expects low‑hundreds of millions in revenue over coming years and warns potential margin dilution.
: Cummins (CMI) shifts capital to high-growth segments while maintaining tech R&D and expanding aftermarket services; capital allocation prioritizes growth areas and aftermarket investment.
